verdicts.note: Points 1 to 4 hold. The draft-07 quotes are verbatim, the PostgreSQL note on extracted timestamps is verbatim, and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING without a target covers all unique indexes. Two corrections. (a) The 'minor wording' claim is wrong. PostgreSQL fills B-tree leaf pages to fillfactor 90 when keys extend the index at the right, while random keys split pages and fragment the index, so a UUIDv7 index is smaller than a UUIDv4 index over the same rows. 'Dizinleri küçük' is defensible against v4 (not against bigint). (b) The Idempotency-Key draft expired on 2026-04-18; it is guidance, not a standard. Also, the proposed CHECK (uuid_extract_version(id) = 7) is outside ON CONFLICT, so a single bad id aborts the whole 200-record insert. It can only be a backstop behind API validation (see misses).
verdicts.correction: Keep 'dizinleri küçük': right-edge inserts fill leaf pages to 90 percent, so the index is smaller than a v4 index. Cite the IETF text as an expired draft. Validate the id format in the API (Zod) so the record alone gets 'ret', and keep the CHECK only as a backstop.

evidence.quote: For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90

The optional ON CONFLICT clause specifies an alternative action to raising a unique violation or exclusion constraint violation error.

verdicts.note: The RFC 7515 signing-input definition is verbatim, and storing the exact bytes once is right. 'The signature and certificate columns are redundant' holds only if the full JWS compact string is stored: the signature is its third segment, not part of the signing input. It does not hold on iPhone. Line 683 signs each record with an App Attest assertion, a CBOR object with its own DER signature plus authenticatorData, verified over SHA256(authenticatorData || SHA256(clientData)). Re-verifying later needs the record bytes, the assertion bytes as received, and the attested public key. Line 589 also says hardware signatures are DER, so they are not standard ES256 JWS signatures, though the exact bytes still re-verify.
verdicts.correction: Store each of these once, as received: the record's exact bytes (or the full JWS compact string) and, for iPhone records, the App Attest assertion bytes. The device row keeps the public key. No separate parsed signature or certificate columns.

evidence.quote: Concatenate authenticatorData and clientDataHash, and apply a SHA256 hash over the result to form nonce. ... Use the public key that you store from the attestation object to verify that the assertion's signature is valid for nonce.
JWS Signing Input: The input to the digital signature or MAC computation. Its value is ASCII(BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)) || '.' || BASE64URL(JWS Payload)).

verdicts.note: The quotes are verbatim, but the conclusion is overstated. 95 percent of records arrive within 24 h (line 830), so block ranges still separate weeks and months, and a month-range report skips most ranges. Only day-level ranges suffer. PostgreSQL also has minmax-multi BRIN operator classes built for outliers like late rows. The recommendation still stands under the plan's 'indexes from real queries' rule: no BRIN up front, and add one on arrival time if a real query needs it.
verdicts.correction: Not 'skips little'. A plain minmax BRIN on record time loses precision for day ranges but still prunes month ranges, and minmax-multi handles late outliers. Defer it anyway.

evidence.quote: While minmax operator class summarizes values from each block range into a single contiguous interval, minmax-multi allows summarization into multiple smaller intervals to improve handling of outlier values.

Also, if the index's autosummarize parameter is enabled, which it isn't by default, whenever autovacuum runs in that database, summarization will occur for all unsummarized page ranges that have been filled

verdicts.note: The PGDATA and VOLUME change is confirmed, and so are 18.6 as the current minor and the advice to run it. The stated consequence is wrong. On 18 and above, the official entrypoint detects a mount or volume at /var/lib/postgresql/data, records it as '(unused mount/volume)', prints the 18+ error and exits 1. The container fails loudly instead of silently writing to an anonymous volume. The fix (one mount at /var/lib/postgresql) stands, and it also keeps pg_upgrade --link possible for the later move to 19.

recommendation_issues.problem: Running CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY 'göç aracının dışında' leaves the index out of the migration history, so fresh databases and the test template database (line 644) never get it. Keep it tracked instead. The release step runs the CONCURRENTLY command first, and the Drizzle migration carries the same CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, so new databases build the index and production skips it. A failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index that IF NOT EXISTS silently accepts (PG docs: 'there is no guarantee that the existing index is anything like the one that would have been created'), so the step must check validity. Second, text plus CHECK beats enum, but changing a CHECK on the large table needs NOT VALID and then a VALIDATE in a separate release, because Drizzle runs all pending files in one transaction (Squawk's constraint-missing-not-valid flags this). Third, enforce the timeouts with Squawk's require-lock-timeout and require-statement-timeout rules rather than by convention.

The uuid version CHECK is not handled by ON CONFLICT, so one bad id aborts the whole batch. Validate the format in the Zod contract first, so only that record gets 'ret', and keep the CHECK as a backstop. Drop the proposed 'dizinleri küçük' wording change (see verdict).
recommendation_tr writes unmeasured figures (3.5 GB, 10 GB) into the plan as if they were facts. Keep only the measurement step (pg_total_relation_size after the k6 run).
The recommendation must also keep the iPhone App Attest assertion bytes. Without them, iPhone records cannot be re-verified, so 'yıllar sonra da yeniden doğrulanabilir' is false for half the fleet.
Testcontainers (line 644) must use the same POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS (builtin C.UTF-8). Otherwise text ordering and comparisons in tests differ from production.

This step is missing from the recommendation: tables created by later migrations get no grants for the app role unless the first migration runs ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE <owner>, or each migration grants explicitly. Keep pg-boss 12 queues unpartitioned (the default, 'every queue's jobs share one table') so that the app role needs no DDL at run time.

'Ek paket gerekmez' is overstated for the fallback. archive_command only runs a shell command, so shipping WAL off the machine (F12) needs a mounted remote path or a copy tool. pg_basebackup --incremental also needs summarize_wal = on, which is off by default ('must be enabled in order to perform an incremental backup').

On the 60 s archive_timeout, the same PG paragraph says 'archived files that are closed early due to a forced switch are still the same length as completely full files. Therefore, it is unwise to use a very short archive_timeout'. pg-boss keeps the database active, so a full segment can be archived every minute, all day. F13 already closes the loss window from the phones, so a few minutes plus pgBackRest compression is the better trade, and the plan should state how far back point-in-time recovery must reach (retention).

'Beklemede' is a decision state (line 205: waiting for confirmation or a settings change), not an evidence flag. Keep it in the decision column next to var, incelemede and ret, or the flag and the decision can contradict each other.

Following Apple's 'greater than the previous assertion' rule in arrival order conflicts with offline-first. Records get per-record 'tekrar dene' (line 127), so an older record can arrive after a newer one was accepted. Any assertion used for another request (time certificate refresh on each app open, line 192) also advances the counter before old offline records are sent. Check counters in seq order, end a device's batch at the first 'tekrar dene', and do not let request assertions advance the record counter (see misses).

The recommendation offers two mechanisms; the plan should pick one. For rare schedule writes and one developer, the counter row is simpler to reason about and to test than xid watermarks, where one long transaction holds xmin back and phones keep re-downloading the same changes. Both rewind on a point-in-time restore (see misses).

misses.finding: ON CONFLICT handles only unique and exclusion violations. Any other constraint error (CHECK, foreign key, NOT NULL) in a multi-row insert aborts the statement and puts the transaction in aborted state. Each send writes up to 200 records in one short transaction (lines 127, 729), phones send in order, and the plan promises per-record results. So one record that trips a database rule fails the whole batch on every retry, and that phone's later records never arrive, which breaks 'Kayıt kaybı 0' and the 95 percent within 24 h target. The researcher's F04 point 4 covers only unique conflicts.

evidence.quote: The optional ON CONFLICT clause specifies an alternative action to raising a unique violation or exclusion constraint violation error.
Moreover, ROLLBACK TO is the only way to regain control of a transaction block that was put in aborted state by the system due to an error, short of rolling it back completely and starting again.

misses.plan_quote: Her gönderim tek kısa veritabanı işlemiyle tek sunucuda karşılanır; k6 ile kanıtlanır.
misses.finding: The official image runs PostgreSQL's conservative defaults (shared_buffers typically 128MB), and Docker gives containers a 64MB /dev/shm, which can make larger report queries fail with 'could not resize shared memory segment'. A k6 run on default settings does not prove the production setup.

evidence.quote: If you have a dedicated database server with 1GB or more of RAM, a reasonable starting value for shared_buffers is 25% of the memory in your system.
the default /dev/shm size for containers is 64MB. If the shared memory is exhausted you will encounter ERROR: could not resize shared memory segment . . . : No space left on device

misses.recommendation_tr: PostgreSQL kabı varsayılan ayarla kalmaz: shared_buffers belleğin yaklaşık dörtte biri olur, Compose'da shm_size en az 256 MB verilir. k6 testini bu üretim ayarlarıyla koşarım; yoksa 'tek sunucu yeter' kanıtı yanıltır.

misses.finding: The plan does not say how the real queries will be seen. pg_stat_statements ships with PostgreSQL (no new package), but it only works when preloaded at server start, and enabling it later needs a restart.

evidence.quote: The module must be loaded by adding pg_stat_statements to shared_preload_libraries in postgresql.conf, because it requires additional shared memory.

misses.recommendation_tr: Gerçek sorguları görmek için pg_stat_statements'ı baştan açarım (PostgreSQL ile gelir, ek paket değil; sonradan açmak yeniden başlatma ister). Dizin kararlarını bu listeye göre veririm.

misses.plan_quote: Dersler ve ders saatleri: gün, saat, derslik, teori ya da uygulama, yoklama süresi.
misses.finding: Lines 116-119 need sections (şube): double major and minor courses keep their own lists, and jointly taught sections share one attendance and one head count. The model has no section entity and no link from a session to several sections, and that link decides how lists and the one-record-per-session rule join.

evidence.quote: Tek yoklama ve tek kafa sayısı (böyle şube varsa).

misses.recommendation_tr: Veri modeline şube eklerim: ders listesi şubeye bağlıdır, bir oturum birlikte işlenen birden çok şubeyi kapsayabilir. 'Bir oturumda bir öğrenciye tek kayıt' kuralı şubeler birleşse de geçerli kalır.

verdict_reason: No finding is high severity and none is refuted. 15 are confirmed and 4 corrected: F04 (UUIDv7 indexes are in fact smaller than v4, and the IETF draft has expired), F07 (iPhone App Attest assertions must be stored too), F08 (BRIN effect overstated; minmax-multi exists) and F19 (the PostgreSQL 18 image exits with an error instead of writing to an anonymous volume). 1 is unverifiable (F06, medium): the size totals are unmeasured hand estimates. The checked items hold; one is incomplete (line 624, UTC for schedule hours). Misses are 3 medium and 8 low. The medium ones: one non-unique constraint error aborts a whole batch and stalls a phone's queue; a restore rewinds the sync version so phones skip changes; App Attest counters checked in arrival order reject valid offline iPhone records. No high-severity miss remains, so the slice passes with these corrections.
